title: codehound: A Zero-Dependency AST Static Analyzer for Concurrency and Resource-Management Defects in Python AI/ML Frameworks
description:
codehound is a zero-dependency static analyzer built on Python's standard-library ast module. It detects six classes of correctness and async-safety defect that recur in production Python AI/ML codebases:

  • CH001 — event-loop-blocking calls inside async functions
  • CH002 — mutable default arguments
  • CH003 — deprecated datetime.utcnow()
  • CH004 — deprecated get_event_loop()
  • CH005 — unclosed file handles
  • CH006 — fire-and-forget tasks eligible for garbage collection mid-run

Each rule is distilled from a defect found and fixed in a widely-used open-source AI/ML framework. Applied to a corpus of 29 popular frameworks, the analyzer identified 1,377 candidate defects; a subset of the resulting fixes were reviewed and merged upstream by project maintainers, providing external validation that the reported defects are genuine rather than false positives.

The archive includes the analyzer source (~750 LOC), its test suite, CI configuration, and the full corpus scan results used for the accompanying empirical study.
